title: Newspaper Act 1908
definition: The Newspaper (Incitement to Offences) Act, 1908, was a draconian legislative measure enacted by the British colonial government to suppress the burgeoning nationalist press, specifically targeting publications that encouraged violence or acts of terrorism during the Swadeshi Movement.
importanceInUpsc: It is a critical component of the 'Press during British Rule' module, frequently tested to evaluate the candidate's understanding of colonial repressive mechanisms and the evolution of the Indian freedom struggle.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Newspaper Act 1908.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
